sermon.title: Laws of Nature and Nature's God
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: In this short teaching Pastor David G. Kincer explains Jefferson’s “laws of nature and of nature’s God” from Bolingbroke and Blackstone as following God in his works and word—the Bible. He says America’s founding and the Declaration rest on Jesus Christ and Bible morals, and warns that lack of this knowledge destroys people.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Short clip (~5 min). Bolingbroke/Blackstone quotations and dates given as spoken; not independently verified in this pass. Hosea 4:6 (“lack of knowledge”) is quoted without naming the reference.

chunks.section_question: What did William Blackstone teach about the law of nature?
chunks.short_answer: He quotes Blackstone’s Commentaries: when the Supreme Being formed the universe and created matter, he established certain laws for plants, animals and vital economy, guided by unerring rules of the Creator. As man depends on his Maker, he must conform to his Maker’s will, and that will is called the law of nature.
chunks.text: To prove it further. That the laws of nature and nature’s God is God in the Bible we’re going to take a look at william Blackstone. The famous commentaries on the laws of England he lived between 1723 and 1780. And he was required reading for all students in America as well as in most European nations. And this is what he says. When the supreme being formed the universe wow. And created matter out of nothing he established certain laws. The progress of plants from seed to root to seed again the method of animal nutrition digestion and secretion and all the branches of vital economy.

faqs.question: When was the phrase “nature and nature’s God” used?
faqs.answer: He says it started in the 1600s and was used for over a hundred years by high officials in government and experts in law.

faqs.question: Who does he quote defining nature and nature’s God?
faqs.answer: He quotes Lord Bolingbroke (1678–1751): the modest inquirer who follows nature and nature’s God makes real progress in discovering divine truths—that equals following God in his works and word.

faqs.question: Why does he cite William Blackstone?
faqs.answer: He says Blackstone’s Commentaries on the Laws of England (1723–1780) was required reading for students in America and most European nations.

faqs.question: Are God’s laws for nature without error?
faqs.answer: From Blackstone he says plants, animal nutrition and vital economy are not left to chance but guided by the Creator’s unerring rules—no mistakes.

faqs.question: What must man conform to, according to Blackstone?
faqs.answer: Because man depends absolutely upon his Maker for everything, he should in all points conform to his Maker’s will, called the law of nature.

faqs.question: What does he say the Declaration of Independence bases separation on?
faqs.answer: He says they based their authority to separate on Jesus Christ, the God of the Bible, and his word the Scriptures.

faqs.question: Why does he quote “for lack of knowledge my people are destroyed”?
faqs.answer: He says it is sad that we lack this founding knowledge of Bible and Christian values in the nation’s beginning.

scriptures.text_nkjv: My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge. Because you have rejected knowledge, I also will reject you from being priest for Me; Because you have forgotten the law of your God, I also will forget your children.

faqs.question: What date does he give for the Declaration?
faqs.answer: He cites the unanimous Declaration of Independence, July the 4th, 1776, and starts the second paragraph “We hold.”
